headline: Deep learning now guides compound, target, and molecular glue discovery
label: Machine Learning Compound Screening
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply graph, attention, and multimodal deep learning to compound and target prioritization.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned molecular representation applied to ligand-target and compound-property prediction, with architectures tailored to each problem. GPCR-Filter couples ESM-3 receptor embeddings with graph neural network ligand encodings through attention, trained on over 90,000 GPCR-ligand pairs. LC-JT-VAE instead conditions a junction tree variational autoencoder on ligase identity to generate synthesizable molecular glues that promote Abeta-42 degradation. Other items extend the same toolkit to adjacent questions: Artemis integrates biomedical knowledge graphs with ChEMBL clinical features for target prioritization, NeuroTDPi adds SHAP interpretation for neurotoxic compound prediction, and DLMVF uses attention over miRNA and drug attributes for miRNA-drug associations. The sodium-iodide symporter study takes a more classical route, pairing docking-based virtual screening with RF, XGB, and SVM models on ECFP4 and CDDD features.
